title: Speed Climbing
primary_metric: combined national-team composite score (team mean climb time + team median climb time, summed across both 4-person teams, in seconds; lower is better)

options.A: Select the team purely on projected race times to maximize the odds of winning gold
options.B: Select the team on demonstrated character, leadership, and long-term development, even if it costs some raw speed

legacy_conversion_note: Source: source/Y3/Session 1/Speed Climbing/Case Study_ Speed Climbing.docx + Guide Notes.docx, read in full. The protagonist (Coach Carlos Chen), gym (The Summit, St. George), the twelve real named climbers with their full timed-trial results (Appendix A), practice/competition histories and six-month progression (Appendix B), and Coach's Notes character profiles (Appendix C) are preserved verbatim from the source docx -- none of this scenario data is invented. The official Nationals team-scoring rule (team mean climb time + team median climb time, lower wins, alternate doesn't count unless substituted) is also verbatim from the source. Per cases/_concepts/LEGACY_DILEMMA_LOCKS_2026-08-20.md (human-approved 2026-08-20), the original's open six-option philosophy prompt is locked to the two real camps the source's own three letters already collapse into: the gym owner's and captains' letters both argue pure-speed selection (Option A); the parents' letter argues character/leadership/development (Option B). The original case gave no explicit team-assignment rule for splitting 8 selected athletes into two 4-person teams -- this conversion adds one (Appendix D's alternating-seed rule, MA2), disclosed as a stated convention rather than left ambiguous, to satisfy Tier 2 P4's no-unstated-convention requirement. The original Appendix B's 'Best Practice Climb Time (last 12 months)' column is, on inspection, actually each climber's most-recent (1-month-ago) progression value, not her true fastest-ever recorded time -- for Ava and Kylie specifically these are two different numbers, since both climbers' six-month trend is getting slower, not faster. This is a real ambiguity in the legacy source (a labeling inconsistency, not a conversion error) and is surfaced explicitly rather than silently resolved: case.md Appendix B carries an explanatory note, and Appendix F's MA1 states and defends the conversion's choice (use most-recent, not all-time-best) as the more defensible predictor of Nationals performance. The Twist (Kylie's practice injury, forcing an alternate-promotion decision) is preserved verbatim from the original Guide Notes. Real-world grounding (current IFSC wall specs and world-record times, USA Climbing's own Youth Speed discipline) was added via WebSearch/WebFetch, since the source docx made no real-world sourcing claims of its own -- these are new appendix material (Appendix E), not corrections to the source.

deliverables.text: A complete roster for both national teams -- all eight athletes selected from the twelve, split into two teams of three competitors plus one alternate each -- built using Appendix A/B's climb-time data and Appendix D's official scoring and team-assignment rules.
A team-composite-score calculation (team mean climb time + team median climb time, per Appendix D's official formula) for each of the two teams, plus the combined total across both.

A consistency analysis: for at least four athletes, the range between their three timed climbs in today's selection trial (Appendix A), with a written explanation of how a single fastest climb and a typical climb can tell different stories.

A percent-improvement calculation using the six-month performance progression data (Appendix B) for at least four athletes, including at least one who improved and one who did not, with a written explanation of what the trend means for team selection.
Two original visual displays: a ranking of all twelve athletes by official selection time, and a six-month trend comparison for at least four athletes.
A written response to the Twist: a recomputed combined team-composite score under the new circumstances, with a numbers-based justification for who replaces whom.

appendices.title: The Summit's U18 Speed Climbing Team: Athlete Files & Coach's Notes

balance.argument_a: Selecting the eight fastest official times produces a combined team-composite score of roughly 30.8 seconds across both teams -- the mathematically lowest score achievable from this pool of twelve, and the only roster that maximizes the odds of a podium finish. Every alternative roster is slower by construction, because Option A is, by definition, the fastest legal roster this data can produce.
balance.argument_b: A character-and-leadership-weighted roster -- built from Appendix C's coaching notes rather than Appendix B's stopwatch alone -- lands at a 32.03-second combined composite, only 3.9% slower than Option A's 30.82-second optimum, not a landslide loss. 6 of the 12 athletes make the team under either philosophy; the real dilemma is only 2 swing seats. For a cost of about 1.2 seconds of combined team time, Option B keeps both team captains (whose leadership the letters themselves argue keeps the whole program together) on the roster, and it rewards the 2 climbers -- Gertrude (+23.3% over 6 months) and Jane (+21.8%) -- whose trend lines are improving fastest, which Option A's single-snapshot metric does not weight at all.
balance.margin_basis: Primary metric = combined national-team composite score (team mean + team median climb time, summed across both teams). Using Appendix B's official practice times and Appendix D's ranking + alternating-seed rule: Option A (8 fastest athletes) = 30.82 s combined. A facilitator-reference Option B roster (character/leadership rubric built from Appendix C, ties broken by speed) = 32.03 s combined. Margin = (32.03 - 30.82) / 30.82 = 3.9%, Option A faster. The character rubric itself is not published to students (Appendix F, MA3) -- this is the facilitator's own worked reference model, not the graded 'correct' rubric; see sensitivity_model.py and FACILITATOR.md.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix A/B's given data and Appendix D's stated rules; case-readiness should re-derive independently via sensitivity_model.py, not just trust this block.

display._note: Rounded-for-prose versions of the figures above, kept as their own keys so FACILITATOR.md's rounded display numbers are checkable (T1-14) rather than drifting from the full-precision values above.

modeling_assumptions.text: This case treats each climber's 'Best Practice Climb Time' (Appendix B) -- her most recent recorded monthly time -- as her official selection time, rather than her single fastest time ever recorded, because current form is a more defensible predictor of Nationals performance than an old personal best. See Appendix F.

Once 8 athletes are selected, teams are assigned by ranking them by official time and alternating seed (1st-2nd-1st-2nd...), with each team's own slowest-of-four becoming its alternate. A fixed, disclosed rule, not a free modeling choice students make themselves. See Appendix D/F.

The case does not publish a pre-built 'character and leadership score.' Turning Appendix C's qualitative coaching notes into a disclosed, defensible rubric is left to the student as part of Option B's pitch. See Appendix F.

sensitivity_note: The primary metric's 3.9% margin is real but built on a facilitator-reference character/leadership rubric (see sensitivity_model.py) whose point weights are themselves a disclosed modeling choice, not a sourced figure -- Tier 2 probe 5 flexes those weights +/-50% to test how much the roster and the margin actually depend on the exact scoring scheme used for Option B. See case-readiness Tier 2 P5 findings once run.
